rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes stride from 256 to 255 in final_mean_kernel's accumulation loop. With batch_size=128 and 256 threads: For any thread tid∈[0,127], the loop executes once (tid<128) then exits (tid+255≥128 and tid+256≥128). For tid∈[128,255], the loop never executes (tid≥128). Both strides produce identical access patterns when batch_size=128.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutant survives because the stride change (256→255) only affects behavior when batch_size exceeds the stride value. With batch_size=128 (fixed), each thread with tid<128 enters the loop exactly once at index tid, then exits because tid+255≥128 (just like tid+256≥128). Threads with tid≥128 never enter the loop in either version. The mutation would only manifest different behavior if batch_size≥256, causing some threads to iterate multiple times with different indices depending on stride. Since batch_size is fixed at 128, the mutation is semantically equivalent under this contract.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract. The behavioral difference only manifests when batch_size > 255, but batch_size is fixed at 128. With batch_size=128, both stride=255 and stride=256 result in each of the first 128 threads accessing exactly one unique batch_means element, producing identical results regardless of input values.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing for GPU kernels should consider whether mutations to loop strides/bounds can be exposed by the fixed shapes in the test contract. When batch_size (128) is less than both stride values (255 and 256), stride mutations in accumulation loops become equivalent. To improve killability, either (1) use batch_sizes larger than typical block sizes, or (2) add shape-parameterized tests that exercise the full range of the kernel's design space.
